Sourdough Ciabatta Baker's Percentage

Cut the slack dough into slippers and barely shape them, so the large holes survive. Leavened with starter rather than a packet of yeast.

Detailed method

Wet slippers leavened with starter. Currently 500 g flour, 82% hydration, 20% starter, 2.2% salt, and 0% yeast. That is 410 g water, 100 g starter, 11 g salt, 1021 g of dough. The starter is itself 100% hydration, the same assumption used for effective hydration. The page shows 83.6% effective hydration. Currently 4 pieces of 255.3 g. Cut them. Do not roll them tight. These times assume you only change the flour amount and keep the percentages the same. Still judge the dough by how it looks and feels.

  1. Starter Use 100 g of starter that is bubbly and has about doubled. That starter is part of the gram total.
  2. Mix Stir 500 g flour, 410 g water, the 100 g starter and 11 g salt until no dry flour remains. At 82% the dough is wet. Fold it in the bowl. Aim for about 24°C (75°F).
  3. Bulk Cover it at about 24°C (75°F) for about 3 to 4 hours. Give it three folds in the first 90 minutes. It is ready when it has grown by about half and looks bubbly.
  4. Cut Tip the 1021 g onto a well-floured tray and cut it into 4 pieces of 255.3 g. Stretch each piece just enough to look like a slipper. The default 1021 g uses a rimmed tray about 40 cm long, 30 cm wide, and 2 cm high. If you change the amount, use a larger tray in proportion or bake in two batches.
  5. Proof Cover the pieces on the tray for 30 to 50 minutes, until they look puffy. With 20% starter, bake them before they spread into a puddle.
  6. Bake Heat the oven to 230°C (450°F). Bake 18 to 24 minutes with steam, until the crust is golden and the slippers feel light. If you have no steam, set a small tray of hot water on the bottom rack. Cool on a rack. Do not press them flat while they are hot.
